title: Affine-local cohomology of derived tensor
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], $P,N$ complexes of $\mathcal O_X$-modules, with $P$ K-flat [def-pc-kflat-complex] and $Q(P),Q(N)$ having quasi-coherent cohomology [def-pc-derived-category]. For an affine open $U\subset X$ and $n\in\mathbb Z$, the restriction to $U$ of $H^n(Q(\operatorname{Tot}(P\otimes N)))$ [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves] is quasi-coherent.

source.place: Tag 08DX, perfect-lemma-quasi-coherence-tensor-product, proof of (1) using (2), and Tag 06Z0

proof.text: Restrict Q(P) and Q(N) to U using the exact over-equivalence functor. Apply schemeDerivedQCoh_openRestriction_iff and underived isQuasicoherent_over to obtain quasi-coherence on U.
Choose module complexes M,L representing these two quasi-coherent derived objects on the affine scheme U, using exists_affine_module_complex_representative.

Use the upstream functorial flat resolution of M to construct a specified K-flat module complex K and quasi-isomorphism K→M. Apply the affine chart tensor computation. Tensor the two representative isomorphisms and compose with that computation to identify the restricted derived tensor with Q of termwise restriction of tilde Tot(K tensor L).

Apply the core affine derived equivalence to Tot(K tensor L), giving quasi-coherent homology of its tilde complex. Compose homologyFunctorFactors and mapHomologicalComplexHomologyIso for exact chart restriction. Underived restriction preserves quasi-coherence, so transport through the tensor model gives quasi-coherent homology of the tensor on U.

The K-flat counit comparison on constant functors identifies Q(Tot(P tensor N)) with Q(P) tensor-derived Q(N). Apply exact open restriction, then the independent-universe tensor restriction comparison. Map through homology and transfer quasi-coherence back. Finally use the forward implication of schemeDerivedQCoh_openRestriction_iff in degree n.
